blocks.text: Histograms dataset ki distribution (qeematein kahan kahan aur kitni hain) dikhate hain. Yeh data ko bins ya intervals (number ki ranges, jaise 50-55, 56-60) mein rakhte hain, jis se pata chalta hai ke har range mein kitni qeematein aati hain.
Misal: Agar dekhna ho ke students ne maths ke exam mein kaisa kiya, to histogram scores ki distribution dikha sakta hai.

blocks.alt: Histogram, title Maths Test Results. Test Scores ke bins 50-55 se 96-100 tak, frequencies 1, 2, 5, 4, 3, 3, 4, 4, 3 aur 2.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.6: Exam scores ki distribution dikhane wale histogram ki misal (kitab ki Figure 5.6 jaisa hamara apna diagram).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Kitab mein is histogram ka title 'Maltis Test Results' chhapa hai, jo printing ki ghalti hai; yahan 'Maths Test Results' likha gaya hai. Histogram mein bars aapas mein jure hote hain kyunke bins lagataar (bina gap ke) hain: 50-55, 56-60, waghaira. Sab se oonchi bar 61-65 ki hai (5 students).
Yeh program scores ko bins (ranges) mein gin kar text histogram banata hai: har * ek student hai. scores ya bin_width badal kar Run karein aur distribution ki shakal badalte dekhein.

scores = [50, 65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 60, 70, 88]
start = 50
bin_width = 10    # 10 means bins 50-59, 60-69, ...

low = start
while low <= max(scores):
    high = low + bin_width - 1
    count = 0
    for s in scores:
        if low <= s <= high:
            count = count + 1
    print(f"{low:>3}-{high:<3} |", "*" * count, count)
    low = low + bin_width

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"scores": das scores; "start = 50" pehle bin (khana / range) ka shuru; "bin_width = 10" har bin ki chaurai.
"low = start": abhi wale bin ki neeche wali had.
"while low <= max(scores):": jab tak bin sab se bare score (95) tak na pohanch jaye, loop chalta rehta hai.
"high = low + bin_width - 1": bin ki oopar wali had, maslan 50 se 59.
Andar wala "for s in scores:" loop har score dekhta hai; "if low <= s <= high:" score is bin mein ho to count 1 barhata hai.
print: bin ki range, phir utne * jitne students, phir ginti. ":>3" aur ":<3" range ko seedh mein rakhte hain.
"low = low + bin_width": agle bin par chale jao (60, 70, ...).
Output: paanch lines: "50-59 | * 1", "60-69 | ** 2", "70-79 | ** 2", "80-89 | *** 3" aur "90-99 | ** 2" (range ke aas paas seedh ke liye kuch extra spaces ke saath). 80s wala bin sab se lamba hai.
Khud try karein: bin_width = 20 kar ke Run karein: sirf teen bins banenge: 50-69 (3), 70-89 (5) aur 90-109 (2).

blocks.prompt: Das scores 50, 65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 60, 70, 88 ko 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s aur 90s ke bins mein rakhein.
blocks.explanation: 50s: 1; 60s: 2; 70s: 2; 80s: 3; 90s: 2. 80s wala bin sab se uncha hai.

items: Histogram: har bin mein kitni qeematein; distribution ki shakal dikhata hai.
